sentences.text:
Sahanaj Khatun @ Sahanaj Khatun Bibi vs The State Of West
Bengal & Ors on 20 February, 2023

Author: Rajasekhar Mantha
Bench: Rajasekhar Mantha
20.02.2023.

Court No.13
Supple Item No. 1
 ap W.P.A. No. 4256 of 2023

Sahanaj Khatun @ Sahanaj Khatun Bibi
 Versus
 The State of West Bengal & Ors.
 Mr. Koustav Bagchi,
 Mr. Debayan Ghosh,
 Ms. Priti Kar.
 ...
For the petitioner.
Despite service of notice on the Government  Pleader, High Court, Calcutta and Sagardighi Police  Station, there is no representation on their behalf.
Affidavit-of-service filed in Court today be taken on  record.
The petitioner's husband is an In-charge of  Sagardighi Assembly Constituency on behalf of Indian  National Congress, a political party.
The petitioner herself is a member of the local  Panchayat Samity representing the Indian National  Congress.

On 18th February, 2023 on allegations under Sections 376 and 417 of the Indian Penal Code, as  ascertained by the petitioner, the petitioner's husband Sahanaj Khatun @ Sahanaj Khatun Bibi vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127932519/
1  was picked up from their residence and taken into  custody.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegation of the de facto complainant being  the respondent no.5 herein is that on a promise of marriage, the petitioner's husband had physical relations with her.
The said respondent no.5 was already married and had two children, the older is 13 years old.
The victim is stated to have left the house of her husband and live with her mother awaiting marriage with the petitioner's husband.
The complaint as far as the petitioner could ascertain is dated 17 th February, 2023.
The petitioner's husband was picked up on the very next day in the late hours.
Counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Bagchi, would submit that the complaint itself is vague and does not disclose the time or the period during which the alleged offence took place.
He further submits that the said incident is vague and, if at all, took place sometimes back.

He also submits that in terms of the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Lalita Kumari - Vs. - Government of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. reported in (2014) 2 SCC Page 1, the delay in lodging of the complaint should have prompted the police to have first made enquiries.

entities.text: Lalita Kumari - Vs. - Government of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. reported in (2014) 2 SCC Page 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court notes that even otherwise a physical relationship based on promise to marriage, cannot mature into an offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code.
The law in this regard is well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

The entire action by the police, as described hereinabove, according to the Counsel for the petitioner is politically motivated by the ruling dispensation to prevent the petitioner's husband from campaigning on behalf of the Indian National Congress.
Be that as it may, this Court is desirous of giving one further opportunity to Sagardighi Police Station to present the case diary before this Court tomorrow at 2:00 P.M.

The petitioner shall serve notice of this order and/or gist thereof to the Officer-in-charge, Sagardighi Police Station, indicating that this matter is taken up for further consideration tomorrow at 2:00 P.M.
In the event the State is not represented tomorrow, it shall be presumed that they have no objection to the prayers made in the writ petition.
List the matter accordingly.
All parties are directed to act on a server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.

(Rajasekhar Mantha, J.)
